body.statement: For every fixed \(K\ge2\), \(q\in\mathbb R^K\), and positive \(R_g,R_e\), \(\lim_{T\to\infty}V_{T,K}(q;R_g,R_e)=V_{\infty,K}(q;R_g,R_e)=R_e^2N_q^2\). For every power of two \(L\ge2d\), \(D_L^{\mathrm G}\in\mathfrak D_{\infty}\), it has at most \(2L^2\) hidden states, and \(\mathcal R_{\infty,K}(D_L^{\mathrm G})=\max\{R_e^2N_q^2,(R_g^2/L)\lambda_{\max}(D_q(M_L+H_d)D_q^{\top})\}\). Consequently, if \(L\ge\max\{2d,B_KR_g^2/R_e^2\}\), then \(\mathcal R_{\infty,K}(D_L^{\mathrm G})=R_e^2N_q^2\).
body.justification: This theorem identifies the global stationary efficiency frontier and supplies a finite-state optimal randomization with a matching spectral lower bound.
body.gap: Tellambura, Guo, and Barton use two deterministic complementary inputs for an information criterion; no checked result proves one-path design-based minimax MSE or equality with the finite-horizon limit.
body.consumer: It gives an implementable long-horizon binary assignment law for individualized impulse-response experiments when treatment counts may remain random.
